provenance: Larry's son's written report to the archive on the evening of 2026-09-12, correcting the archive's description of VD-0004 (which had read the left-hand mark on the flight line as a crossed-out aeroplane). His son was present while Larry drew the sheet that afternoon and did not take notes; this is his account from memory, in his own words, not Larry's.
text: The plane he crossed out isn't a plane, the X are the helicopter blades in the photo for Rosethorn 007 and next to it is a plane. The helipcopter was the first thing he drew as he was explaining where Rosethorn 007 was located in relation to the buildings around it.
hold: His son's account says where Rosethorn 007 stood on VD-0004, which the open (validate) question asks him to say himself. Held off the pages until he has been asked it.
researchNotes: Said of the left-hand mark on the flight line of VD-0004: the strokes are rotor blades, not a crossing-out, and the drawing is the helicopter Rosethorn 007, drawn first, while Larry was explaining where it stood relative to the buildings. "In the photo" is read as the drawing; his son was describing the sheet. It settles the three characters above the helicopter, which had been withheld because a rounded character could be a zero or a letter O: in Larry's account this is Rosethorn 007, the call sign he has named unprompted four times, so the label is recorded as 007. It also places the aircraft, in his telling, on the flight line of the base he calls Ton Son Nhut, beside a de Havilland Beaver and an L19. Ledger #28, #35.
